gen-dafont-klill-fs-fira-sans: Uniform strokes, curves kept wide apart: that's Klill. Fira Sans carries the paragraphs with s curves that swing wide at both ends and a tall x-height, so text keeps flowing without snagging.
gen-dafont-klill-fs-nunito: Nunito ends its strokes well away from the stem, with big round bowls. But Klill draws with one nib throughout, so the page moves from professional headings into a friendlier body.
gen-dafont-klill-fs-public-sans: Trustworthy, with a flat gray hum of constant line weight. Klill is happiest holding its curve endings apart, while Public Sans earns its keep with a hefty body and broad counters.
gen-dafont-klill-general-sans: Clean, smooth, and steady from the first letter to the last. General Sans fills each line with curves that glide around bends and a tall x-height, and next to Klill it reads smoothly paragraph after paragraph.
gen-dafont-klill-switzer: Curve endings held well apart, that's the Klill look. Switzer, tubular and tall-waisted with c tips that never creep toward touching, matches that openness, and the shared build is what makes this pair hang together.
gen-dafont-nasalization-fs-rowan: Rowan is literary and friendly, with thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones. Rowan follows Nasalization, a display face of short ascenders and floating letters, and keeps paragraphs easygoing in feel.
gen-dafont-ozone-fs-neco: Neco reads with authority, a measured swell from hairline to stem and letters that never seem to pinch shut. Beneath geometric headings in Ozone, text feels dignified and unhurried.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-fs-asap: Asap reads smoothly, with c forms like open arcs and a body height nearly matching the capitals. But Rounded Elegance does the warm, inviting part, its monoline strokes crowding close, while Asap does the readable work.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-rowan: Rowan reads warm and literary, its thin strokes about half the weight of thick ones. Rowan gives dreamy Starborn, all blank space and dark lowercase stripes, something grounded to lean on.
gen-dafont-stilu-switzer: Blown-glass lowercase bowls give Stilu its luxurious shape, terminals never closing in. Switzer is tubular and wire-like with a tall waist line, so paragraphs move with a Swiss, approachable ease.
